title: highmarsh home factor dosing instruction
instruction:
You are Agnes Zubair, the RN nurse coordinator at Highmarsh Foundry Children’s Hemostasis Service in New York, and you have one teaching session left with Iris Underwood, 68, before she drives four hours home with her seven-year-old grandson and ward, Aleksy Schuyler, for the winter. Iris will be giving his factor VIII without another trained adult present, including overnight. Renata Zuniga has asked you to revise the current handout because it reads like a classroom explanation rather than something Iris can dose from at 2 a.m., and the dispensing practice is changing mid-winter. Aleksy weighed 24.6 kg on 15 November 2026. His current prescribed plan is 25 IU/kg for a suspected joint or muscle bleed and 50 IU/kg for a suspected head, neck or abdominal bleed or major injury. Show projections for confirmed weights of 27.5 kg and 30 kg as well, but do not present a projected dose as permission to use it before that weight is confirmed. His current supply has whole vials labeled 262 IU, 536 IU and 1,048 IU. From 1 January 2027, Anvilcross Engineering Specialty Pharmacy expects to dispense only the 536 IU and 1,048 IU strengths. Partial vials are not used, and a selected whole-vial combination must not provide less than the calculated dose. Bohdan Haldorsen’s pharmacy review also says the sheet must leave product ordering, substitution, storage and reconstitution details to the pharmacy label and pharmacy team rather than making new pharmacy instructions. Prepare an editable, large-print home factor dosing and bleed-response instruction sheet that Iris can navigate quickly, covering both the transition stock and the expected end state without making her reconcile two documents. Keep it to no more than two pages, written for a caregiver with no clinical background, and do not turn it into a general infusion manual. Do not invent telephone numbers, additional prescribed rates or additional vial strengths; use clearly labeled editable blanks where local contact details are needed. Apply New York practice boundaries as of 15 November 2026. Write the finished file into the top level of the working directory using exactly the filename `aleksys_home_factor_guide.docx`.

---

Write your finished work to the **top level of the current working directory**, using exactly these filenames:

- `aleksys_home_factor_guide.docx` — Editable, large-print home factor VIII dosing and bleed-response instruction sheet for a nonclinical caregiver. (Must be no more than two rendered pages; must address current and post-transition vial availability in one document; must remain editable; must not invent contact numbers, dose rates or vial strengths; must be written into the top level of the working directory using the exact filename.)

Nothing outside those filenames is collected. A correct file written anywhere else, or under any other name, scores zero.

gold.text:
ALEKSY SCHUYLER
HOME FACTOR VIII DOSING & BLEED-RESPONSE GUIDE
For Iris Underwood • Use during the current plan; this sheet is education, not a new prescription.
IF A HEAD / NECK / ABDOMINAL BLEED OR MAJOR INJURY IS POSSIBLE: call 911 / emergency services now. Give the prescribed 50 IU/kg factor promptly if it is available and you can give it safely—do not delay transport, assessment, or emergency care.

1  QUICK PATH AT 2 A.M.

1. Identify the event. Joint or muscle symptoms use 25 IU/kg. Head, neck or abdominal symptoms, or a major injury, use 50 IU/kg (emergency). If unsure, call the hemostasis team—do not guess.
2. Confirm today’s weight in kilograms before choosing a row. Do not estimate, round, or use a future projection. If the confirmed weight is not 24.6, 27.5, or 30 kg, call for a new dose.
3. Check the stock-period box below. Read and verify the IU potency printed on every vial label. If labels do not match that box, do not substitute or improvise; call the hemostasis or pharmacy team.
4. Use only whole vials. Do not split a vial or save a partial vial for a later dose. The listed total may be higher than the calculated target so the dose is not under the target.
2  CURRENT STOCK  |  262 IU + 536 IU + 1,048 IU

Use this box while those three labeled strengths are in the home. Calculated IU = confirmed kg × prescribed IU/kg.

“Whole vials” means use the listed combination in full. It must meet or exceed the calculated dose; never split or save a partial vial.
3  EXPECTED PHARMACY CHANGE  |  FROM 1 JANUARY 2027

Anvilcross Engineering Specialty Pharmacy expects to dispense only 536 IU and 1,048 IU. This is a planned change, not a guarantee that a different label cannot arrive. Use the actual labeled stock supplied; if it differs, call before choosing.

Projected rows (27.5 kg and 30 kg) are planning aids only. They become usable only after that exact weight is confirmed and the treating team’s plan remains current.
4  RECOGNIZE THE EVENT

Do not wait for visible swelling. Early treatment and a phone call matter.
POSSIBLE JOINT BLEED  →  25 IU/kg
Pain, warmth, tingling, stiffness, guarding a joint, a limp, or less movement than usual. Swelling may be absent.
POSSIBLE MUSCLE BLEED  →  25 IU/kg
New pain or swelling with a change in movement or function; a limb may feel tight or be hard to use. Concerning limb symptoms need prompt advice.

5  EMERGENCY RESPONSE  |  50 IU/kg

Treat any blow to the head as a possible serious bleed—even if Aleksy looks well at first. Watch for worsening headache, vomiting, unusual sleepiness, confusion, seizure, weakness, or loss of consciousness.
Neck warning signs: swelling, voice change, trouble breathing or swallowing. Abdominal warning signs: significant pain, swelling, repeated vomiting, faintness, or a hard/tender belly. Major injury means substantial trauma or bleeding that worries you.
Call 911 / emergency services for serious head, neck, or abdominal symptoms, breathing trouble, loss of consciousness, seizure, collapse, or other life-threatening change. Do not delay transport for factor, a callback, or diagnostic certainty.
While help is being arranged, give the prescribed 50 IU/kg factor if it is available and you can give it safely. Notify the hemostasis team promptly after emergency help is activated or factor is given.
If you are unsure which category applies, call urgently rather than guessing. Repeat or additional doses, a changed rate, or a changed treatment plan require direction from the hemostasis treatment team or authorized prescriber.
6  SAFETY STOP

Stop administration and call 911 for trouble breathing, facial or throat swelling, widespread hives, faintness, or collapse (possible severe allergic reaction). If venous access cannot be obtained promptly or the dose cannot be completed safely, stop repeated attempts and seek help; never delay emergency care.
7  BEFORE / AFTER THE DOSE

Before use: read the pharmacy label and follow the pharmacy team’s instructions for ordering, product substitution, storage, and reconstitution. This sheet does not add temperatures, shelf-life rules, diluent volumes, infusion rates, or product instructions.
Check the product is not expired. Record vial potency and lot information. Record the date and time, suspected bleed or injury, body site or symptoms, selected dose, and whether emergency services or the clinical team was contacted.
8  CONTACTS & TEACH-BACK

Round-the-clock hemostasis team
Name/phone: __________________________________________
Specialty pharmacy (Anvilcross)
Name/phone: __________________________________________

Before leaving teaching, Iris can say: (1) which signs use 25 vs 50 IU/kg; (2) how she confirms weight and stock period; (3) how she reads each vial’s IU label; and (4) when she calls 911, the hemostasis team, or the pharmacy team.
Caregiver notes / event log:  Date/time __________  Event/site or symptoms ______________________________  Dose/vials __________________  Lot(s) __________  Help contacted __________________

spec.professional_context: A pediatric hemostasis nurse is converting a reviewed teaching handout into a caregiver-facing tool for independent home use. The guide must remain mathematically accurate while accommodating a planned pharmacy transition and respecting the boundary between nursing education, prescribing and pharmacy instructions.
difficulty_sources: Maintaining exact weight-based dosing and whole-vial rounding across two bleed categories, three weights and two inventory states
Making projected future rows useful without presenting them as current authorization
Balancing rapid caregiver navigation against a two-page large-print limit
Providing safe bleed-response education while respecting prescribing and pharmacy boundaries
Revising explanatory material into an operational tool that can be used without live support

authoring_plan.solver_instance: Create a compact caregiver-facing home factor VIII dosing and bleed-response guide from the patient-specific facts embedded in the request, using professional nursing knowledge for bleed recognition, escalation, teach-back and scope boundaries.
authoring_plan.intended_verdict: A strong solution is mathematically exact, usable during a stressful overnight event, explicit about the transition and end state, and bounded so it does not become a prescription or pharmacy handling manual.
required_imperfections_and_tensions: The caregiver must use current inventory during a transition and later use an inventory from which one strength has disappeared; the document must support both states without requiring two guides.
Projected weights are needed for planning, but they are not permission to use a row before that weight is confirmed.
Whole-vial rounding creates substantial overfill in some end-state cases; the guide must preserve the prescribed minimum rather than smoothing the arithmetic into an underdose.
The nurse owns caregiver education and response guidance but not product substitution, dispensing, storage, reconstitution specifications, new dose rates or repeat-dose authorization.
No real telephone numbers are available, so the usable artifact needs conspicuous editable contact fields rather than invented details.
gold_relationships: For each weight and indication, calculated IU equals confirmed weight in kilograms multiplied by the prescribed IU/kg rate.
The lower-dose calculated targets derive from multiplying each stated weight by 25 IU/kg.
The emergency calculated targets derive from multiplying each stated weight by 50 IU/kg.
A qualifying vial selection uses whole vials only and has total labeled potency greater than or equal to the unrounded calculated target.
Among qualifying selections from the applicable stock set, use the lowest total potency; if totals tie, use the selection with fewer vials.
Current-stock combinations may use only 262 IU, 536 IU and 1,048 IU vials.
Post-transition combinations may use only 536 IU and 1,048 IU vials.
Projected-weight rows are planning outputs and become actionable only after the corresponding weight is confirmed.
If actual labels differ from the listed strengths, the caregiver does not extrapolate or substitute and instead contacts the treatment or pharmacy team.
Emergency response should allow prompt factor administration when safely possible while never delaying emergency services or transport.
Repeat dosing, altered dose rates and treatment-plan changes remain with the authorized clinical team.
professional_content_expected: Early, caregiver-recognizable joint and muscle bleed signs.
A low threshold for treating head trauma as potentially serious, including delayed neurologic symptoms.
Recognition of serious neck and abdominal symptoms and major injury.
A clear uncertainty path that does not require caregiver diagnosis.
Emergency-service triggers and instructions not to delay transport for infusion completion, callback or diagnostic confirmation.
Severe allergic-reaction response and a safe boundary when venous access or administration cannot be completed.
After-dose documentation covering event, time, site or symptoms, dose, vial potency, lot information and contacts made.
A brief teach-back or self-check appropriate to the final teaching session.
required_vocabulary_and_local_convention: The exact filename is supplied in the request.
The patient-specific weights, rates, vial strengths, transition date, jurisdiction and as-of date are supplied in the request.
Contact details must be represented by editable blanks labeled for the round-the-clock hemostasis service and specialty pharmacy.
The document should distinguish current stock from the expected post-transition stock using caregiver-visible wording; no private transition code is required.
authoring_plan.reference_files: None. All patient-specific and local facts required for scoring are contained in the solver-visible request; remaining expectations are standard professional knowledge for caregiver education about home factor therapy.
authoring_plan.offline_validation: A reference DOCX can be authored with python-docx, rendered with LibreOffice and checked offline. All vial totals can be generated by enumerating nonnegative whole-vial combinations from the applicable stock set and selecting the minimum total meeting each calculated target, breaking equal-total ties by vial count. The rendered reference can fit within two pages using readable large-print tables, short action blocks and compact editable contact and teach-back fields.

deliverables.description: Editable, large-print home factor VIII dosing and bleed-response instruction sheet for a nonclinical caregiver.
constraints: Must be no more than two rendered pages; must address current and post-transition vial availability in one document; must remain editable; must not invent contact numbers, dose rates or vial strengths; must be written into the top level of the working directory using the exact filename.
